nodes.name: Shinjuku
nodes.description: Big hub around the world's busiest train station: skyscrapers, neon, shopping, and nightlife like Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho.

nodes.name: Yodobashi Camera
nodes.description: Huge electronics chain; the Shinjuku West flagship spans several buildings of cameras, gadgets, watches, and more.

nodes.name: Nakano Broadway
nodes.description: Retro multi-floor shopping arcade packed with anime and manga collectibles (incl. many Mandarake shops) and one of Tokyo's biggest clusters of used and vintage watch dealers.

nodes.name: Shibuya crossing
nodes.description: The famous scramble crosswalk where huge crowds cross from every direction at once.

nodes.name: Takeshita Street
nodes.description: Harajuku's crowded pedestrian street of kawaii fashion, crêpes, youth culture, and animal cafes (samoyed dogs, micro-pigs, etc.)

nodes.name: Imabari Towel (Minami-Aoyama)
nodes.description: Official shop for Imabari towels, Japan's certified premium cotton towels, from handkerchiefs to bath sheets; near Omotesando.

nodes.name: glänta (Omotesando)
nodes.description: Ring studio where you can make your own rings or order a custom one from a craftsman; workshop rings go home the same day.

nodes.name: Senso-ji Temple
nodes.description: Tokyo's oldest temple, entered through the giant-lantern Kaminarimon gate and Nakamise-dori.

nodes.name: Bar Centifolia
nodes.description: Theatrical cocktail bar in Azabu-Juban run by champion bartender Yuzo Komai.

nodes.name: Ginza Tsutaya Books
nodes.description: Beautiful art-focused bookstore on the 6th floor of Ginza Six, with rare art and photography books on a 30 m bookshelf, an art gallery, and a café.

nodes.name: Nihonbashi Nishikawa
nodes.description: Flagship of the centuries-old bedding maker Nishikawa, where staff measure your neck and build a custom pillow on the spot; you can also try its mattresses and pillows.

details.openHoursText: 11:00–20:00 — ⚠ COREDO Nihonbashi closes ~Oct 2026 for redevelopment, reopens as Tokyo Midtown Nihonbashi "autumn 2027" (timing vs trip uncertain). Fitting also at Hiroo (Tokyo) & Daimaru Shinsaibashi (Osaka)

nodes.name: teamLab Planets
nodes.description: Immersive digital art museum where you walk barefoot through water and mirrored light rooms.

nodes.name: Ghibli Museum
nodes.description: Hayao Miyazaki's whimsical Studio Ghibli museum with exclusive short films.

nodes.name: JAL Sky Museum
nodes.description: Japan Airlines' museum and guided walk through a working aircraft maintenance hangar at Haneda Airport.

nodes.name: Gotokuji Temple
nodes.description: Temple said to be the birthplace of the maneki-neko, filled with thousands of white beckoning-cat figurines left by visitors.

nodes.name: Tokyo DisneySea
nodes.description: Disney park unique to Tokyo, themed around ports of the sea, incl. the Fantasy Springs area (Frozen, Tangled, Peter Pan); often called the best Disney park.

nodes.name: Shiraito Falls
nodes.description: Wide curtain of countless thin waterfalls spilling over a cliff on Mt. Fuji's southwest side, near Fujinomiya.

nodes.name: Lake Kawaguchiko
nodes.description: The most visited of the Fuji Five Lakes, with Mt. Fuji views across the water, lakeside cafés, and onsen hotels.

details.openHoursText: Outdoor; retro sightseeing bus loops the lake

nodes.name: Chureito Pagoda
nodes.description: Five-story pagoda on a hillside above Fujiyoshida: the classic postcard view with Mt. Fuji behind it.

nodes.name: Ghibli Park
nodes.description: Studio Ghibli park recreating film settings (Howl's, Totoro, etc.)

nodes.name: TSUTAYA BOOKSTORE (Noritake Shinmachi)
nodes.description: Beautiful bookstore in Aeon Mall Noritake Garden, famous for a two-story lit bookshelf reflected in a mirrored ceiling so it looks endless; Starbucks inside.

nodes.name: Gion
nodes.description: Kyoto's geisha district of wooden teahouses and lantern-lit lanes like Hanamikoji.

nodes.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
nodes.description: Thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mt. Inari.

nodes.name: Kinkaku-ji
nodes.description: The Golden Pavilion: a Zen temple covered in gold leaf, reflected in the pond in front of it.

nodes.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
nodes.description: Walking path through towering bamboo in western Kyoto.

nodes.name: Nishiki Market
nodes.description: Narrow covered food market known as "Kyoto's Kitchen": pickles, skewers, sweets, and kitchen knives.

nodes.name: Byodoin Omotesando (tea shop street)
nodes.description: Short street of historic matcha shops and cafés — Nakamura Tokichi, Itoh Kyuemon and Tsuen (founded 1160) are all within a few minutes of each other, selling matcha, soft serve and tea sweets.

nodes.name: Amanohashidate
nodes.description: 3.6 km pine-covered sandbar across a bay, one of Japan's Three Scenic Views; tradition is to view it upside down between your legs.

nodes.name: Nara Park
nodes.description: Large park where over a thousand free-roaming deer bow for deer crackers.

nodes.name: Dotonbori
nodes.description: Canal-side strip of neon signs and street food (takoyaki, okonomiyaki), home of the Glico running man sign.

nodes.name: Universal Studios
nodes.description: Universal Studios Japan, incl. Super Nintendo World and Harry Potter.

nodes.name: Den Den Town
nodes.description: Osaka's answer to Akihabara in Nipponbashi: anime, figures, retro games, and electronics.

nodes.name: Shinsaibashi-suji
nodes.description: Long covered shopping arcade running north from Dotonbori.

nodes.name: Umeda Sky Building
nodes.description: Two skyscrapers joined at the top by the Floating Garden Observatory, an open-air rooftop ring with 360° views over Osaka.

nodes.name: Tsutenkaku Tower
nodes.description: Retro observation tower and symbol of the old-school Shinsekai neighborhood, known for kushikatsu; home of the lucky Billiken statue and a tube slide down the side.

nodes.name: Harukas 300
nodes.description: Glass-walled observation deck on the top floors of Abeno Harukas, one of Japan's tallest buildings, about 300 m up with views across Osaka.

nodes.name: Ikoma Sanjo Amusement Park
nodes.description: Retro amusement park on top of Mt. Ikoma (642 m) with views over Osaka and the Nara Basin; its Flying Tower plane ride (1929) is Japan's oldest ride still running. Reached by dog- and cat-shaped cable cars.

nodes.name: Katsuoji Temple
nodes.description: Mountain temple of "winning luck," covered in thousands of daruma dolls left by visitors; a 6-stamp rally around the grounds builds up a full daruma picture on a postcard.

nodes.name: Cup Noodles Museum Osaka Ikeda
nodes.description: Museum at the birthplace of instant ramen, where you design your own cup and choose the soup and toppings at the My Cup Noodles Factory.

nodes.name: Seongsu
nodes.description: Former factory area turned trendy: cafés in converted warehouses, pop-up stores, and indie brands.

nodes.name: Starfield Library (COEX)
nodes.description: Open library in the middle of COEX Mall, with 13 m bookshelves rising around a central seating plaza.

nodes.name: Starfield Library (Suwon)
nodes.description: Bigger sibling of the COEX library inside Starfield Suwon mall (opened 2024), with 22 m bookshelves spanning four floors under a glass ceiling.

nodes.name: Gamcheon Culture Village
nodes.description: Hillside village settled by Korean War refugees, now known for colorful painted houses, murals, and hanbok rentals.

nodes.name: Ben Thanh Market
nodes.description: Central covered market for street food, souvenirs, and clothes.

nodes.name: Ba Na Hills
nodes.description: Mountaintop resort reached by a long cable car, with a French-village replica and gardens.

nodes.name: Old Town
nodes.description: UNESCO-listed old trading port: lantern-lit streets, street food, tailors, riverside cafés.

nodes.name: Fujian Assembly Hall
nodes.description: Ornate Chinese assembly hall and temple built by Fujian merchants.

nodes.name: Old Quarter
nodes.description: Dense maze of streets historically named for trades, packed with street food and shops, near Hoan Kiem Lake.

nodes.name: Beer street
nodes.description: Ta Hien Street: a lively corner of tiny plastic stools and cheap fresh beer (bia hoi).

nodes.name: Mua Caves
nodes.description: About 500 steps up to a dragon statue with sweeping views over the Tam Coc rice fields.

nodes.name: Da'an District
nodes.description: Upscale central district with cafés, cocktail bars, and the Yongkang Street food area.

nodes.name: Daan Forest Park
nodes.description: Large leafy park, often called Taipei's Central Park.

nodes.name: Jiufen Old Street
nodes.description: Narrow hillside lanes of snack stalls, teahouses, and red lanterns.

nodes.name: Bic Camera
nodes.description: Major electronics and camera chain, right by Shinjuku Station's west exit. They also sell lots of watches!

nodes.name: Love Hotel Hill
nodes.description: Dogenzaka slope packed with themed love hotels, plus clubs and live music venues.

nodes.name: Samoyed Cafe Moffu
nodes.description: Café where you hang out with fluffy Samoyed dogs (no other breeds); free treats to feed them and free drinks. Branches on Takeshita Street and elsewhere in Harajuku.

nodes.name: Onitsuka Tiger (Omotesando)
nodes.description: The brand's largest flagship in Japan, with Japan-exclusive models; the NIPPON MADE shop for its fully made-in-Japan line is next door.

nodes.name: Kappabashi Street
nodes.description: Tokyo's "Kitchen Town": a long street of shops selling Japanese knives, tableware, and plastic food samples.

nodes.name: Uniqlo Ginza
nodes.description: Uniqlo's 12-floor Ginza flagship, with a RE.UNIQLO STUDIO counter that embroiders bags and clothes with your own design. It's also 2-3x cheaper than the US.

nodes.name: Anamori Inari Shrine
nodes.description: Inari shrine with a tunnel of ~1,000 red torii gates up a small hill — a pocket Fushimi Inari; the aviation-safety / airport-guardian shrine.

nodes.name: Oishi Park
nodes.description: Flower park on Lake Kawaguchiko's north shore, framing Mt. Fuji across the lake.

nodes.name: Ryoan-ji Temple
nodes.description: Zen temple with Japan's most famous rock garden; a short trip from Kinkaku-ji.

nodes.name: Miffy Sakura Kitchen
nodes.description: Miffy-themed bakery and gift shop near the bamboo grove, selling Miffy-shaped anpan and pastries plus exclusive Kyoto pottery and kitchen goods.

nodes.name: Kiyomizu-dera Temple
nodes.description: Hillside temple with a huge wooden stage overlooking Kyoto, reached via the old Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka lanes.

nodes.name: Pontocho
nodes.description: Narrow lantern-lit alley along the Kamo River, lined with restaurants, bars, and teahouses.

nodes.name: Todai-ji
nodes.description: Temple with a giant bronze Buddha inside one of the world's largest wooden buildings in Nara Park.

nodes.name: Osaka Castle
nodes.description: Iconic castle (a modern rebuild) with a museum inside, surrounded by moats and a big park.

nodes.name: Kuromon Market
nodes.description: "Osaka's Kitchen": covered market with fresh seafood, wagyu skewers, and street snacks.

nodes.name: Namba Yasaka Shrine
nodes.description: Shrine whose stage is a giant lion head with an open mouth, said to swallow bad luck.

nodes.name: Hannam
nodes.description: Upscale area with designer boutiques, galleries, and good restaurants; next to Itaewon.

nodes.name: Hwaseong Fortress
nodes.description: UNESCO-listed 18th-century fortress wall circling old Suwon, with grand gates, watchtowers, and a walkable path along the top of the wall.

nodes.name: Haedong Yonggungsa Temple
nodes.description: Buddhist temple built right on the seaside cliffs.

nodes.name: Cu Chi Tunnels
nodes.description: Huge underground tunnel network used in the Vietnam War.

nodes.name: Golden Bridge
nodes.description: Walkway held up by two giant stone hands, located inside Ba Na Hills.

nodes.name: Quan Cong Temple
nodes.description: Colorful Chinese temple honoring the general Guan Yu, across from the central market.

nodes.name: Train street
nodes.description: Narrow residential lane where trains pass inches from cafés.

nodes.name: Trang An
nodes.description: UNESCO-listed rowboat tours through limestone karsts and river caves.

nodes.name: National Palace Museum
nodes.description: World-class collection of Chinese imperial art and artifacts, incl. the famous Jadeite Cabbage.

nodes.name: Jiufen Teahouse
nodes.description: Traditional teahouse in a historic building, with tea service and mountain views.

nodes.name: Camera Town
nodes.description: Cluster of new and used camera shops by Shinjuku Station's west exit, incl. Map Camera and vintage dealers.

nodes.name: Shibuya
nodes.description: Youth fashion and nightlife district around Shibuya Station and its famous scramble crossing.

nodes.name: Shibuya Sky
nodes.description: Open-air rooftop observation deck on Shibuya Scramble Square, looking straight down on the crossing.

nodes.name: Meiji Jingu
nodes.description: Large shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji, set in a forest behind giant wooden torii gates.

nodes.name: PORTER Omotesando
nodes.description: Flagship of Porter (Yoshida & Co.), the Japanese bag maker, on a quiet Omotesando backstreet; full range of shoulder and sling bags, backpacks, and luggage.

nodes.name: GU Ginza
nodes.description: Five-floor global flagship of GU, Uniqlo's cheaper and trendier sister brand, a couple of minutes from Uniqlo Ginza. It's also 2-3x cheaper than the US.

nodes.name: Mt. Fuji Panoramic Ropeway
nodes.description: Short cable car up Mt. Tenjo on Lake Kawaguchiko's east shore, with a viewing deck looking across the lake to Mt. Fuji.

nodes.name: Sanjusangen-do
nodes.description: Temple hall about 120 m long holding 1,001 golden statues of Kannon.

nodes.name: Otagi Nenbutsu-ji
nodes.description: Mossy hillside temple with 1,200 stone figures, each with its own funny expression, carved by amateur visitors.

nodes.name: Kasuga Taisha
nodes.description: Shrine famous for its thousands of stone and bronze lanterns, in the forest at the east end of Nara Park.

nodes.name: Hozenji Yokocho
nodes.description: Stone-paved lantern alley by Dotonbori, home to a moss-covered Fudo statue that visitors splash with water for luck.

nodes.name: Itaewon
nodes.description: Seoul's most international district: global food, bars, and nightlife.

nodes.name: Oryukdo Skywalk
nodes.description: Glass-floored U-shaped walkway over a cliff, looking out to the Oryukdo islets.

nodes.name: Bui Vien Walking Street
nodes.description: Backpacker nightlife strip in District 1: packed bars, loud music, and street food.

nodes.name: Monkey Mountain
nodes.description: Son Tra Peninsula: forested hills with ocean viewpoints and rare red-shanked douc langurs.

nodes.name: Japanese Covered Bridge
nodes.description: Hoi An's symbol: a small covered bridge from the early 1600s.

nodes.name: Tam Coc
nodes.description: Rowboat ride along a river through rice paddies and caves between limestone cliffs.

nodes.name: Wang Tea
nodes.description: Tea roaster in Dadaocheng since 1890; tastings, tea for sale, and tours of the roasting workshop.

nodes.name: Teapot Mountain
nodes.description: Short but steep hike near Jinguashi to a teapot-shaped rock with panoramic coastal views.

nodes.name: Cha no Ikedaya
nodes.description: Small family-run Japanese green tea shop, run by a certified tea appraiser, known for its rich matcha soft serve; also sells loose-leaf tea and matcha powder.

nodes.name: JINS
nodes.description: Japanese eyewear chain known for affordable prescription glasses; the Shibuya store is the flagship.

nodes.name: Itoya (G.Itoya)
nodes.description: Ginza's landmark stationery store, in business since 1904: about a dozen floors of pens, notebooks, paper, cards and desk goods, each floor themed, with a café at the top.

nodes.name: Philosopher's Path
nodes.description: Quiet stone path along a canal, linking temples between Ginkaku-ji and Nanzen-ji.

nodes.name: Nakatanidou
nodes.description: Mochi shop famous for its lightning-fast mochi pounding shows, selling fresh mugwort (yomogi) mochi.

nodes.name: Haeundae Blueline Park
nodes.description: Coastal rail park; the Sky Capsules are small colorful pods that run on an elevated track along the sea.

nodes.name: Saigon Central Post Office
nodes.description: French-colonial post office from the late 1800s, next to the Notre-Dame Cathedral.

nodes.name: Marble Mountain
nodes.description: Limestone hills with caves, pagodas, and viewpoints, on the way between Da Nang and Hoi An.

nodes.name: Kawaguchiko Ryokan
nodes.description: Fuji-view room with a private onsen (not booked yet)

nodes.name: Bar Benfiddich
nodes.description: Tiny 17-seat apothecary-style bar where Hiroyasu Kayama makes cocktails from herbs he grows on his own farm; No. 18 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2025.

nodes.name: Hands Shibuya
nodes.description: Multi-floor lifestyle store (formerly Tokyu Hands) for well-made everyday things: household goods, tools, travel gear, kitchenware, stationery, bath and beauty.

nodes.name: MUJI Ginza
nodes.description: MUJI's world flagship: several floors of simple household goods, clothing, travel gear and food, with a MUJI hotel and restaurant in the same building.

nodes.name: Nijo Castle
nodes.description: Shogun's castle with ornate painted rooms and "nightingale floors" that squeak to warn of intruders.

nodes.name: Seokbulsa Temple
nodes.description: Mountain temple on Geumjeongsan with large Buddhist figures carved into the rock face.

nodes.name: My Son Sanctuary
nodes.description: Ruins of ancient Cham Hindu temples in the jungle; a UNESCO site.

nodes.name: Omoide Yokocho
nodes.description: Alley of tiny yakitori stalls and izakayas by Shinjuku Station's west exit, nicknamed "Memory Lane."

nodes.name: Shibuya Loft
nodes.description: Hands' trendier sibling: stationery, cosmetics and skincare, character goods and seasonal gift floors.

nodes.name: Gwangalli Beach
nodes.description: Beach lined with cafés and restaurants, known for its coffee street and evening views.

nodes.name: Lady Buddha
nodes.description: Tall white Buddha statue at Linh Ung Pagoda on Son Tra, overlooking the bay.

nodes.name: Golden Gai
nodes.description: A few narrow alleys packed with around 200 tiny bars, each seating only a handful of people, many with their own quirky theme.

nodes.name: Asakusa
nodes.description: Old-Tokyo neighborhood around Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest temple, and the souvenir stalls of Nakamise-dori.

nodes.name: Dongbaekseom Island Coastal Promenade
nodes.description: Easy seaside walking trail around a small wooded island, with views of Busan's skyline.

nodes.name: Dragon Bridge
nodes.description: Dragon-shaped bridge over the Han River that breathes fire and water.

nodes.name: Kabukicho
nodes.description: Tokyo's neon nightlife district of bars, restaurants, and clubs, home to the life-size Godzilla head on Hotel Gracery.

nodes.name: Akihabara
nodes.description: "Electric Town": electronics, anime, manga, retro games, and maid cafés.

nodes.name: Haewol Observatory
nodes.description: Crescent-shaped observation deck opened in 2024, reaching 134 m out over the sea off Haeundae.

nodes.name: My Khe
nodes.description: Da Nang's long, wide city beach.

nodes.name: Don Quijote
nodes.description: Chaotic discount chain stacked floor to ceiling with snacks, souvenirs, cosmetics, and oddities.

items.title: Breakfast
items.note: Immigration+customs varies (\~1-2 hours). Breakfast at Haneda Airport Garden; add Suica to phone (Apple/Google Wallet) and forward bags to the hotel (takkyubin)

items.title: Breakfast
items.note: Near Shinjuku Station. Option: forward big bags straight to the Nagoya hotel (takkyubin) and bring only an overnight bag

items.title: Chureito Pagoda (sunrise)
items.note: Taxi \~15 min at \~5:30; \~400 steps up. Audrey's pick
1 Keikyu stop (\~5 min) from Haneda; 1,000-torii tunnel; drop bags first

items.title: Drop bags at ryokan
items.note:
Hours: Check-in usually \~15:00; bags OK earlier

Fuji-view room with private onsen
Only if watch/lens not found elsewhere
\~2 monorail stops from Terminal 3 (Shin-Seibijo). Earliest tour 9:30 (arrive \~9:00); closed Wed & Fri; reserve ahead, popular
Knives, whetstone, scissors, tongs, chopsticks, ceramics; knife-buying is slow; most shops \~10 AM–5 PM, closed Sun — do in the morning
North shore; Fuji across the lake
Watch / camera / Zojirushi; tax-free counter queue \~10–20 min
Go \~3:30–4 PM: tour-group queues thin out, and sunset (\~5:15 mid-Oct) lands right before the last descent

items.title: Dinner (ryokan kaiseki)
items.note:
Hours: Usually \~18:00–19:00 start

Confirm dinner time when booking
Sunset capstone (\~5 PM Oct); book timed ticket
